slides.title: Interview ka [[Monster]] ques
points: Problem: Wo users dhundo jo **3+ days** lagatar login karein
Sirf COUNT se kaam nahi chalega ❌
slides.note: FAANG interviews mein ye logic baar baar pucha jaata hai

slides.title: Sample table: [[Logins]]
slides.note: Yahan User 1 ne 3 din lagatar login kiya hai ✅

slides.title: Simple [[Magic]] logic
points: **ROW_NUMBER** se har user ko numbering do
Agar streak hai, toh result **constant** aayega
slides.note: Bole toh: 10 Jan - 1 = 9 Jan, 11 Jan - 2 = 9 Jan. Same diff!

slides.title: Likhte hain [[Full Query]]
slides.code:
WITH t AS (
  SELECT u_id, l_dt,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER(PARTITION BY u_id
      ORDER BY l_dt) AS rn
  FROM logins
)
SELECT u_id FROM t
GROUP BY u_id, (l_dt - rn)
HAVING COUNT(*) >= 3;

slides.title: [[Breakdown]] Clause-wise
points: **CTE (t)**: Har user ki dates ko rank kiya
**l_dt - rn**: Consecutive dates ko group kiya
**HAVING**: Jinka count 3 ya usse zyada hai
slides.note: Ye logic tabhi chalta hai jab dates unique hon per user per day

slides.title: [[Final Result]] dekho
slides.note: User 2 filter ho gaya kyunki uska streak 3 nahi tha

slides.right: ROW_NUMBER se grouping karke COUNT check karna
slides.why: COUNT se pata nahi chalta ki dates **lagatar** hain ya beech mein gap hai ❌

points: GROUP BY + HAVING se count check karo
